successors.name: British Colonial Empire
successors.text: Essequibo and Demerara, official British territory from 13 August 1814 and part of British Guiana from 21 July 1831

ledger.x: 1621: the West India Company takes the colony ('Established as a Dutch West India Company colony: 1621'; 'The administration of the West Indian Company as well as the governor of the entire colony settled here in 1621').
1781 (24 February): British privateers take Essequibo and Demerara.
1782: the British lose the colony to the French.
1796: 'In 1796 it was permanently occupied by the British.'
1802: the Treaty of Amiens (27 March 1802) returns it: 'the Netherlands received the Essequibo colony for a short time, from 1802 to 1803'.
1803: 'after that the British again occupied it during the Napoleonic Wars' (the governor table has Robert Nicholson from September 1803).
1812 (28 April): under British occupation 'Joined with Demerara to form Demerara-Essequibo'.
1814 (13 August): 'Essequibo became official British territory on 13 August 1814 as part of the Treaty of London'.

wars.name: British, French and Dutch contest for Essequibo
wars.outcome: British privateers took the colony in February 1781, the French held it from 27 February 1782 to February 1783, the Dutch were restored by the 1783 Treaty of Paris, the British took it permanently in 1796, returned it for 1802-1803 and held it to the 1814…

certainty.note: Plantation coast and river posts; the pages give no frontier, area or survey.
